raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou, so my thinking here is pretty straightforward — wheat then maize, same as my father, same as my neighbors. Everyone around here does this rotation, and I have 12 mu of contracted land. I'm not going to experiment. The county extension office pushes the same thing, and the grain station buys both crops reliably.

For wheat, I plant in late October. I'll use the Jimai 22 variety — it does well in our soil and I've used it for a few years. I apply compound fertilizer before plowing and topdress urea in March at jointing. Groundwater irrigation is how we survive here — I pump at least 4 times over the season. Aphids and powdery mildew show up every year so I spray twice.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I get maize in the ground fast — within a few days. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, machine-planted. I skip deep plowing to save time and diesel; just rotary the stubble under. I top-dress urea twice. Rain in July and August usually helps but I'll pump 2 times to be safe. I spray once for fall armyworm — that's been a problem the last couple years.

I expect around 450 kg/mu wheat and 550 kg/mu maize. That's what I got last year roughly.
